question: Assume today is 2026-08-17. You know nothing published after this date. Estimate the seasonally adjusted annual rate of privately-owned housing starts in the United States in August 2026 (the number of housing units at an annual rate, as in '1,300,000'), as it will be first reported in the U.S. Census Bureau and HUD Monthly New Residential Construction release.

target.what: Seasonally adjusted annual rate of privately-owned housing starts in the United States for August 2026, covering all privately owned residential units (single-family and multifamily) that began construction during the month, as first estimated by the U.S. Census Bureau and HUD.
target.unit: housing units at a seasonally adjusted annual rate
target.publisher: U.S. Census Bureau and U.S. Department of Housing and Urban Development (HUD)
target.cadence: monthly, in the Monthly New Residential Construction release
target.caveats: Working interpretation: private housing starts only, excluding publicly owned units; all structure types; national total; SAAR rather than the unadjusted August count. Alternative definition: total housing starts including public units. Target month is future/partially observed at the 2026-08-17 cut

candidates.hypothesis: The August 2026 private starts SAAR will be anchored by the most recent published private starts level and recent momentum, with August seasonal factors and historical month-to-month volatility defining a plausible range.
candidates.data_to_find: Monthly private housing starts SAAR for 2024 through the latest release published on or before 2026-08-17 (likely June 2026 data unless July data were released earlier), including first and revised estimates; single-family and multifamily splits; historical August private starts and Census seasonal adjustment factors for August; release schedule confirming latest available month.

candidates.hypothesis: Private housing starts are constrained by recent private building permits and the backlog of authorized-but-not-started units, so August starts should be near a lagged conversion of permits plus backlog drawdown.
candidates.data_to_find: Private housing units authorized by building permits SAAR for recent months through latest pre-cutoff release; permits by single-family and multifamily; stock of housing units authorized but not started; historical starts-to-permits ratios by structure type and lag.

candidates.hypothesis: For a given month, private starts approximately equal private completions plus the net change in private units under construction, so recent completions and under-construction stocks can constrain the implied August starts flow.
candidates.data_to_find: Private housing completions SAAR and private units under construction for recent months; monthly changes in under-construction stock; definitions and any demolition/adjustment notes needed to apply the stock-flow identity to Census starts.
search_hints: housing starts completions under construction identity

candidates.hypothesis: Private starts are the sum of single-family and multifamily starts, whose drivers differ; estimating each component separately reduces error from volatile multifamily projects.
candidates.data_to_find: Latest single-family and multifamily private starts SAAR and permits; NAHB/Wells Fargo Housing Market Index; multifamily completions, rental vacancy, and absorption indicators; mortgage rates and apartment financing conditions around August 2026.
search_hints: single family multifamily housing starts SAAR 2026

candidates.hypothesis: Single-family starts respond to new-home sales, inventory of homes under construction, and mortgage rates; weak or strong demand signals should shift the single-family component relative to its recent baseline.
candidates.data_to_find: New single-family home sales SAAR, months supply, and inventory of new homes under construction for recent months; 30-year fixed mortgage rates in July-August 2026; builder incentives and order trends if available.
search_hints: new single family home sales 2026 months supply

candidates.hypothesis: Real residential construction activity, construction employment, and material use provide a cross-check on whether starts are running near capacity or are constrained by labor and materials.
candidates.data_to_find: Census residential construction spending for recent months; residential construction employment; lumber, cement, and other material price or supply indicators; any builder reports on labor and lot availability.

candidates.hypothesis: Weather, mortgage-rate moves, material costs, tariffs, and regional disruptions in August 2026 could push starts away from the recent trend; measurable exposure should be used to adjust or widen the estimate.
candidates.data_to_find: 30-year mortgage rate path in July-August 2026; extreme weather or hurricane landfalls affecting homebuilding regions; lumber/tariff and building-material price changes; builder surveys mentioning delays or cancellations.

candidates.hypothesis: Published professional forecasts and consensus estimates for August 2026 housing starts provide a comparison anchor, though they may rely on the same recent Census data and should not be treated as independent observations.
candidates.data_to_find: Forecasts for August 2026 private or total housing starts from Reuters consensus, Fannie Mae, MBA, NAHB, Wells Fargo, Trading Economics, or similar; any prediction-market contract on US housing starts around August 2026.

methods.rationale: Uses the same latest starts anchor p18 but explicitly applies the observed late-June-to-late-July mortgage-rate increase as a modest headwind. methods.rationale: Demand-based decomposition: estimate single-family starts from new-home sales p19 and a starts-per-sale ratio, then divide by the single-family share implied by one minus the multifamily share. It provides a route that does not directly use the latest starts level, but it depends on two assumptions and on June sales being a useful August proxy. Failure modes include a large multifamily project, a shift in builder spec-home behavior, or sales-to-starts timing lags.

assumptions.name: August-to-June private starts ratio
assumptions.rationale: June 2026 private starts p18 are the latest observed level. June new-home sales p19 versus p21 are below a year earlier and months' supply p25 is high, while the 30-year mortgage rate rose from p35 to p30; these point to a slight August decline relative to June. The range reflects Census 2024 average month-to-month SA starts volatility p1 (about 6.4%) over roughly two months and the larger multifamily volatility p10.
assumptions.applies_when: The June 2026 starts level p18 remains a valid anchor for August and there is no large August shock beyond normal monthly noise.
assumptions.falsified_by: July or August starts, permits, or under-construction data showing a trend far above or below June, or a large August mortgage-rate or weather shock.

assumptions.name: mortgage-rate pass-through to private starts
assumptions.rationale: Used as 1 - a2*(p30/p35 - 1). Housing starts are interest-rate sensitive, but the observed window is only late June to late July, so only partial pass-through is assumed. The range allows weak to strong short-run sensitivity.
assumptions.applies_when: The rate change from p35 to p30 is a relevant signal for August starts, with no larger offsetting demand or supply shock.
assumptions.falsified_by: Evidence that starts are insensitive to mortgage rates over this horizon or that the p30-p35 change is not representative of August financing conditions.

assumptions.name: single-family private starts per new single-family home sold
assumptions.rationale: New-home sales p19 are an annual-rate demand flow. Single-family starts are typically somewhat larger than current sales because builders start spec homes and homes sold before start; with p18 total starts and p19 sales, the total starts-to-sales ratio is above two, implying a single-family ratio around 1.5 if multifamily is roughly one-third of starts. The range reflects uncertainty in that split.
assumptions.applies_when: June 2026 new-home sales p19 is a usable demand proxy for single-family starts in August, and the single-family-to-sales relationship is near its recent range.
assumptions.falsified_by: June or July 2026 single-family starts or sales data showing a materially different starts-to-sales ratio.

assumptions.name: multifamily share of total private housing starts
assumptions.rationale: Multifamily (2+ unit) starts are volatile and are not separately observed in the kept points. A one-third share is used so that p19 times a3 divided by one minus this share gives total private starts. The range reflects the wide historical swing in multifamily share and p10 volatility.
assumptions.applies_when: The August 2026 multifamily share is within the recent historical range and is not dominated by a single large project.
assumptions.falsified_by: July or August 2026 structure-type starts showing multifamily far outside the assumed share.

assumptions.name: August-to-June private starts ratio
assumptions.rationale: Anchor p18 is June 2026 private starts. p1 shows total starts average month-to-month absolute change 6.44% SA in 2024 and p10 shows multifamily 16.41%, so a two-month move of roughly 9-13% is plausible. p30/p35 shows mortgage rates up about 17 bp, p19/p20 shows June SF sales only 10k above May, and p25 shows 9.3 months' supply; these point to a small decline rather than a boom. The ratio is not a level assumption.
assumptions.applies_when: August 2026 conditions remain near the June-July trend and no large weather/credit shock hits starts.
assumptions.falsified_by: A July 2026 starts print far from 1.4M or evidence of a large August shock.

assumptions.name: mortgage-rate pass-through to private starts
assumptions.rationale: Maps the p30/p35 rate ratio into a proportional starts adjustment. A 17 bp rise is small; pass-through is lagged and uncertain. 0.5 means the rate ratio effect is halved; range admits near-zero to strong response.
assumptions.applies_when: The July rate increase is a useful proxy for August financing conditions.
assumptions.falsified_by: Evidence that starts are insensitive to mortgage rates or that a much larger August rate move dominates.

assumptions.name: single-family private starts per new single-family home sold
assumptions.rationale: p19 June 2026 new SF sales 628k; p18 total private starts 1.427M and p74/p75 historical split imply SF starts around 0.95M if MF share is about one-third, giving a ratio near 1.5. p25 9.3 months' supply is above balanced 6 months, so the value should be at the lower end; p54 24% of March sales not started supports starts running above current sales.
assumptions.applies_when: Builders keep starting homes in line with current sales and sold-not-started backlog.
assumptions.falsified_by: A Census SF/MF starts split showing SF starts per sale outside 1.2-1.8 or a sharp inventory correction.

assumptions.name: total-to-single-family starts ratio adjustment, 2026 vs March 2024
assumptions.rationale: p74/p75 gives March 2024 total/SF starts ratio 1,321/1,022=1.293. p76/p74 shows MF share then about 22%; p81/p79 shows MF permit share about 30%. If August 2026 MF share is near one-third, total/SF ratio should be near 1.49, about 1.15 times the 2024 ratio. Range covers MF share from low to high.
assumptions.applies_when: Multifamily's share of private starts is not radically different from the late-2024/2026 range.
assumptions.falsified_by: Current SF/MF split showing multifamily share near the 2024 22% level or far above one-third.

assumptions.name: August private starts to June private completions ratio
assumptions.rationale: p16 June completions 1.392M; p18 June starts 1.427M gives a June ratio of 1.025. p16/p17 shows completions rising 45k from May, while p14 shows under-construction stock changes slowly (1.13% average monthly). A ratio near 1.0 is a physical-flow anchor, with uncertainty from unobserved net under-construction change.
assumptions.applies_when: The net change in private units under construction between June and August is not large.
assumptions.falsified_by: Evidence of a large drawdown or build-up in units under construction, or a July completions print far from 1.4M.

methods.label: m1

p18.role: June 2026 private housing starts SAAR in the United States, the latest observed anchor before the August 2026 target month

a1.role: dimensionless ratio of August 2026 private starts SAAR to the June 2026 private starts SAAR, reflecting two months of trend, mortgage-rate, and sales conditions

methods.rationale: Anchor route: June 2026 private starts p18 times a1, a dimensionless two-month change factor. Uses the latest published private starts. Shared dependency: both target and anchor come from the same Census series; a July revision or August shock is missing. a1 range reflects p1/p10 volatility and p19-p30-p35 conditions. Coverage is full private starts SAAR.

methods.label: m2

p18.role: June 2026 private housing starts SAAR in the United States, the latest observed anchor before the August 2026 target month

a2.role: positive dimensionless pass-through coefficient from the mortgage-rate ratio to private housing starts

p30.role: 30-year fixed mortgage rate for the week of July 30, 2026, representing recent financing costs before the August target month

p35.role: 30-year fixed mortgage rate for the week of June 25, 2026, the baseline financing rate near the June starts observation

methods.rationale: Mortgage-rate-adjusted anchor: p18 times (1 - a2*(p30/p35 - 1)). p30 and p35 are 30-year rates July 30 vs June 25. This is not an independent level forecast; it adjusts the same June anchor for the modest rate rise. Fails if starts respond to rates with long/variable lags or if p18 is revised.

kept.name: August-to-June private starts ratio
kept.rationale: Anchor p18 is June 2026 private starts. p1 shows total starts average month-to-month absolute change 6.44% SA in 2024 and p10 shows multifamily 16.41%, so a two-month move of roughly 9-13% is plausible. p30/p35 shows mortgage rates up about 17 bp, p19/p20 shows June SF sales only 10k above May, and
kept.applies_when: August 2026 conditions remain near the June-July trend and no large weather/credit shock hits starts.
kept.falsified_by: A July 2026 starts print far from 1.4M or evidence of a large August shock.

kept.name: mortgage-rate pass-through to private starts
kept.rationale: Maps the p30/p35 rate ratio into a proportional starts adjustment. A 17 bp rise is small; pass-through is lagged and uncertain. 0.5 means the rate ratio effect is halved; range admits near-zero to strong response.
kept.applies_when: The July rate increase is a useful proxy for August financing conditions.
kept.falsified_by: Evidence that starts are insensitive to mortgage rates or that a much larger August rate move dominates.

kept.name: single-family private starts per new single-family home sold
kept.rationale: p19 June 2026 new SF sales 628k; p18 total private starts 1.427M and p74/p75 historical split imply SF starts around 0.95M if MF share is about one-third, giving a ratio near 1.5. p25 9.3 months' supply is above balanced 6 months, so the value should be at the lower end; p54 24% of March sales not s
kept.applies_when: Builders keep starting homes in line with current sales and sold-not-started backlog.
kept.falsified_by: A Census SF/MF starts split showing SF starts per sale outside 1.2-1.8 or a sharp inventory correction.

kept.name: total-to-single-family starts ratio adjustment, 2026 vs March 2024
kept.rationale: p74/p75 gives March 2024 total/SF starts ratio 1,321/1,022=1.293. p76/p74 shows MF share then about 22%; p81/p79 shows MF permit share about 30%. If August 2026 MF share is near one-third, total/SF ratio should be near 1.49, about 1.15 times the 2024 ratio. Range covers MF share from low to high.
kept.applies_when: Multifamily's share of private starts is not radically different from the late-2024/2026 range.
kept.falsified_by: Current SF/MF split showing multifamily share near the 2024 22% level or far above one-third.

kept.name: August private starts to June private completions ratio
kept.rationale: p16 June completions 1.392M; p18 June starts 1.427M gives a June ratio of 1.025. p16/p17 shows completions rising 45k from May, while p14 shows under-construction stock changes slowly (1.13% average monthly). A ratio near 1.0 is a physical-flow anchor, with uncertainty from unobserved net under-cons

The estimate for the seasonally adjusted annual rate of privately-owned housing starts in the United States for August 2026 is 1,377,831 housing unit/year (80% model-based interval 768,497 to 2,470,303 housing unit/year). This covers all private single-family and multifamily units, national total, SAAR.

The anchor is June 2026 private starts of 1,427,000 housing units at seasonally adjusted annual rate, carried forward by a two-month change factor (0.97, range 0.6846 to 1.369). Supporting routes adjust that anchor for the mortgage-rate rise from 6.49% to 6.66% (0.5), build single-family starts from June new sales of 628,000 houses per year using the March 2024 total/SF split (1,321,000 housing units at seasonally adjusted annual rate, 1,022,000 housing units at seasonally adjusted annual rate) with ratios 1.5 and 1.15, and cross-check against June completions of 1,392,000 housing units at seasonally adjusted annual rate via 1. Only the observed points are data; the ratios are analyst assumptions. The four methods were combined with equal weights (25%, 25%, 25%, 25%); no backtest errors were available.

The main risk is that the June anchor is preliminary and may be revised, and August shocks are unobserved. The interval reflects input uncertainty only. A July revision and August permit data would most improve it.

Key assumptions (proposed by the analyst model, not observed; code samples each one between the bounds shown):
- a1 August-to-June private starts ratio: 0.97 ratio, range 0.6846 to 1.369 (range widened by code); used by m1. Overturned by: A July 2026 starts print far from [n]M or evidence of a large August shock.
- a2 mortgage-rate pass-through to private starts: 0.5 ratio, range 0.1 to 1.5; used by m2. Overturned by: Evidence that starts are insensitive to mortgage rates or that a much larger August rate move dominates.
- a3 single-family private starts per new single-family home sold: 1.5 ratio, range 1.039 to 2.078 (range widened by code); used by m3. Overturned by: A Census SF/MF starts split showing SF starts per sale outside [n]-[n] or a sharp inventory correction.
- a4 total-to-single-family starts ratio adjustment, 2026 vs March 2024: 1.15 ratio, range 0.8078 to 1.616 (range widened by code); used by m3. Overturned by: Current SF/MF split showing multifamily share near the 2024 [n] level or far above one-third.
- a5 August private starts to June private completions ratio: 1 ratio, range 0.704 to 1.408 (range widened by code); used by m4. Overturned by: Evidence of a large drawdown or build-up in units under construction, or a July completions print far from [n]M.

by_construction: Only URLs leave the searcher (code regex); extractor, judge and final prompts never contain search result titles, snippets or the searcher's text. This holds by construction and is not measured.
residual_risks: The searcher sees post-cutoff search results and chooses which URLs are fetched, so page selection can be conditioned on the answer; only the URLs leave the searcher, and in backtests every fetched page is a snapshot dated <= as_of.
Live pages are used only when as_of is today; in backtests every page is an archived snapshot dated <= as_of.
The leak sentinel only catches registered official values in common formats, not paraphrased or derived numbers.
The model's own training data (knowledge cutoff unpublished) can include history before as_of; it cannot include the target if the target was published after the model's release.
Wayback snapshots are captured by a third party; a snapshot date <= as_of proves the content existed by then.
Assumption values are proposed by the judge model from its own knowledge, which can include the target's history before as_of; code checks their form, not where the number came from.
